title: Deterministic linear representations of transversal matroids
formal:
Does there exist a uniform deterministic algorithm that, given any finite bipartite graph with its two sides specified, constructs a rational matrix representing its transversal matroid in polynomial bit time?

Precisely, let \(a,b\) be nonnegative integers and let
\[
G=([a],[b],E),\qquad E\subseteq[a]\times[b],
\]
where the two labeled sides are disjoint copies and \([0]=\varnothing\). Let \(r(G)\) be the maximum size of a matching in \(G\). The required output is one explicit matrix
\[
M\in\mathbb Q^{\,r(G)\times a}
\]
whose column \(j\) corresponds to vertex \(j\) on the first side, such that
\[
\forall S\subseteq[a]\quad
\left[\exists\text{ injective }f:S\to[b]\ 
       \forall j\in S\ (j,f(j))\in E\right]
\ \Longleftrightarrow\
\left[\text{the columns }(M_{\ast j})_{j\in S}
       \text{ are linearly independent over }\mathbb Q\right].
\]
The same matrix must satisfy this equivalence for all subsets simultaneously.

With the encodings and deterministic machine model below, the algorithmic assertion is
\[
\exists A\ \exists C,d\in\mathbb N_{\ge1}\ 
\forall a,b\in\mathbb N\ \forall E\subseteq[a]\times[b]\quad
\exists y\in\{0,1\}^{\ast}\ 
\bigl(
\operatorname{HaltWithin}(A,\operatorname{enc}(G),y,C(L(G)+1)^d)
\land \operatorname{Correct}(G,y)
\bigr).
\]
Here \(A\) is one fixed finite deterministic program, \(L(G)\) is the input's bit length, and \(\operatorname{Correct}\) checks the full matrix requirement above. The constants do not depend on the graph or its rank. This formulation makes explicit the rational-field and bit-complexity setting surrounding the source question; it does not ask for representations over every finite field or permit unit-cost arithmetic on unbounded numbers.
why: This asks whether randomness can be removed from a basic translation between matching constraints and linear algebra. Such representations support matroid algorithms and, through related gammoid representations, several central preprocessing and cut-representation results. A polynomial-time construction would supply one exact algebraic representation of all independence relations without random choices. A negative result would establish a computational obstruction to this widely used translation, despite the existence of small rational representations.
status_note: The inspected 2016 textbook manuscript explicitly asks for deterministic polynomial-time construction in its rational, polynomial-bit representation setting. The MFCS 2025 primary paper still calls this a longstanding open problem and proves a quasipolynomial-time construction instead. A bounded primary-source check through 16 September 2026 found no verified resolution; the inspected 2026 transversal-matroid kernel result has a different, randomized output guarantee. The public progress uses a quasipolynomial bound supported by the 2025 proof without inheriting its inconsistent sharper rank-only entry-bit statement. This is a formulation and theorem-scope review, not an exhaustive literature certificate or Lean proof verification.

importance.reason: A central derandomization problem for translating ubiquitous bipartite matching constraints into one exact linear representation. Its connections to gammoids, representative sets, cut representations and several important kernelization problems give it broad algorithmic consequences. The 2025 quasipolynomial construction highlights a substantial remaining polynomial-time barrier. This assessment replaces the unassessed midpoint and reflects those consequences rather than the textbook source or age alone.

sentences: A bipartite graph defines a transversal matroid by declaring a subset on its first side independent when it can be matched to distinct vertices on the second side.
The task is to construct one explicit rational matrix whose corresponding columns are linearly independent exactly for those subsets.
The question asks for one uniform deterministic algorithm with polynomial bit running time, including the full binary output.

Randomized polynomial-time representations and deterministic quasipolynomial-time representations are known, while polynomial-time derandomization would support important matroid and preprocessing algorithms.
A complete Lean answer must prove such a construction works on every bipartite graph or prove that no deterministic algorithm meets the stated polynomial bound.

definitions:
A finite bipartite graph has two disjoint labeled vertex sets, here \([a]=\{1,\ldots,a\}\) and a separate copy of \([b]=\{1,\ldots,b\}\). An edge is a pair in \(E\subseteq[a]\times[b]\), so there are no parallel edges. A matching is a set of edges no two of which share an endpoint. Its size is its number of edges, and \(r(G)\) is the maximum matching size, including zero for an edgeless graph.

A subset \(S\subseteq[a]\) is independent in the transversal matroid of \(G\) when some matching covers every vertex in \(S\). Equivalently, there is an injective function \(f:S\to[b]\) with \((j,f(j))\in E\) for each \(j\in S\). These independent subsets form the matroid; the task does not receive an explicit list of all such subsets or an additional oracle.

For a matrix \(M\in\mathbb Q^{r(G)\times a}\), its columns indexed by \(S\) are linearly independent precisely when
\[
\forall(\lambda_j)_{j\in S}\in\mathbb Q^S\quad
\left[
 \forall i\in[r(G)]\ \sum_{j\in S}\lambda_jM_{ij}=0
\right]
\ \Longrightarrow\
\left[\forall j\in S\ \lambda_j=0\right].
\]
The empty family of columns is independent. A zero-row matrix is allowed when \(r(G)=0\); its nonempty column families are dependent. In particular, empty sides and isolated vertices are valid inputs. Matrix columns remain labeled by all \(a\) first-side vertices, including isolated ones. The required representation is an actual rational matrix, with no indeterminates, unevaluated expressions or collection of alternative matrices.

Encode \(G\) by the binary string \(1^a0\,1^b0\) followed by its \(ab\) adjacency bits, ordered first by the first-side label and then by the second-side label. Thus
\[
L(G)=a+b+2+ab.
\]
This explicit encoding includes isolated vertices. Polynomial time in this encoding is polynomial time in the size of an explicit graph presentation; it is not time in a compressed specification of exponentially many vertices.

To specify the output encoding, for a nonnegative integer \(k\), let \(\operatorname{bin}(k)\) be its ordinary binary expansion without leading zeros, with \(\operatorname{bin}(0)=0\). Let \(\ell(k)\) be this expansion's length and put
\[
\operatorname{code}(k)=1^{\ell(k)}0\,\operatorname{bin}(k).
\]
A signed integer \(p\) is encoded by one sign bit followed by \(\operatorname{code}(|p|)\), where the sign bit is one exactly for a negative integer; zero has sign bit zero. A rational number is encoded as such a signed numerator \(p\) followed by \(\operatorname{code}(q)\) for a positive denominator \(q\), and denotes \(p/q\). Fractions need not be reduced. A matrix output consists of \(\operatorname{code}(r(G))\), then \(\operatorname{code}(a)\), then the \(r(G)a\) rational entries in row order, with no further bits. The predicate \(\operatorname{Correct}(G,y)\) means that \(y\) has this valid encoding and its decoded matrix satisfies the independence equivalence for every \(S\subseteq[a]\). Thus the polynomial running-time requirement includes writing every numerator and denominator bit.

The computational model is a deterministic multitape Turing machine with one read-only binary input tape, finitely many work tapes, and a binary output stream. The finite program, finite tape alphabets, and number of work tapes are fixed independently of the input. Tape cells are indexed by nonnegative integers; initially the heads are at cell zero, work tapes are blank, and the input string is followed by blanks. A step reads the symbols under the heads, changes the finite control, writes at most one symbol on each work tape, moves each head by at most one cell, and appends at most one bit to the output. A requested move left from cell zero leaves that head at zero. A designated halt state ends the computation. There is no randomness, advice or oracle access. All preprocessing and output steps count. The predicate \(\operatorname{HaltWithin}(A,x,y,T)\) means that \(A\), on input \(x\), halts after at most \(T\) steps with exactly output \(y\). Invalid input strings impose no requirements.

Requiring integer constants \(C,d\ge1\) expresses the usual polynomial-time existence condition: larger integer constants cover any fixed polynomial bound. The row count \(r(G)\) fixes a standard representation convention; the source notes that representations can be taken to have one row per rank. The question requires no prescribed numerical upper bound on individual matrix entries beyond the polynomial number of bits that can be written in polynomial time.
answer_criterion:
Give a complete mathematically correct proof checked in Lean of the formal algorithmic assertion or of its full logical negation.

A positive answer must specify one deterministic finite program \(A\) and constants \(C,d\in\mathbb N_{\ge1}\), and prove that for every encoded bipartite graph it halts within \(C(L(G)+1)^d\) bit steps and outputs one correctly encoded rational matrix. Correctness must prove both directions of the independence equivalence for every subset of first-side vertices in the same output matrix. Existence of a suitable matrix for each graph without a uniform polynomial-time construction is insufficient, as is a bound counting only arithmetic operations without controlling bit costs and output length.

A negative answer must prove
\[
\forall A\ \forall C,d\in\mathbb N_{\ge1}\quad
\exists a,b\in\mathbb N\ \exists E\subseteq[a]\times[b]\quad
\neg\exists y\in\{0,1\}^{\ast}\ 
\bigl(
\operatorname{HaltWithin}(A,\operatorname{enc}(G),y,C(L(G)+1)^d)
\land\operatorname{Correct}(G,y)
\bigr).
\]
Thus, for each proposed program and polynomial bound, some valid graph makes it run too long, fail to halt, produce an invalid encoding, or produce a matrix violating the required equivalence. The defeating graph may depend on the program and bound. The negative claim is computational; it does not assert that a transversal matroid lacks a rational representation.

A randomized construction, a quasipolynomial-time construction, or a construction only for bounded rank does not by itself establish the requested positive assertion. A lower bound for one method or a conditional obstruction does not prove the unrestricted negative assertion unless it also proves the missing general claim or hypothesis. This is an exact algorithm-existence target; numerical \(1/100\) approximation does not replace the required proof.

context_blocks.text: The textbook defines the independent sets by bipartite matchings and gives a randomized polynomial-time construction over the rationals. Immediately after discussing the polynomial bit length of its integer entries, it asks for a deterministic polynomial-time construction. This card fixes that rational, bit-complexity interpretation explicitly.

The representation must preserve every independent set in a single matrix. The existence of rational representations is known; the unresolved issue is constructing them deterministically within polynomial bit time from the bipartite graph.

The MFCS 2025 paper gives a deterministic construction in quasipolynomial time. In terms of the total vertex count \(N\), its construction has time and output length bounded by \((N+2)^{O(\log(N+2))}\), while the polynomial-time question remains open in that source.

The same paper documents applications to gammoid representations, cut representations and deterministic quasipolynomial-time preprocessing for several parameterized problems. These results make the representation question useful beyond testing a single matching constraint, while leaving polynomial time as a distinct endpoint.

Downloaded the actual 30 May 2016 author manuscript as transversal-rep-book2016.pdf/.txt. Read PDF pp. 395–400, especially §12.1.4 and Thm12.3 at pp. 398–399. The theorem outputs integer entries and explicitly represents over Q. Its next paragraph discusses exponential numerical values with polynomial bit length and polynomial bit arithmetic before posing deterministic polynomial time. Thus Q and bit cost are recovered from the original scope; the draft does not substitute arbitrary finite fields, symbolic rational-function entries or unit-cost infinite-precision arithmetic.

The saved graph question permits all finite bipartite graphs with the two sides provided. Chosen unary side sizes plus adjacency bits explicitly include isolated vertices and are polynomially equivalent in size to a conventional explicit adjacency-list presentation. Empty sides are handled. The graph input does not include all independent sets, a bases list, rank advice or a proposed representation.

The rank-row output convention follows §12.1.1, printed p. 380/PDF p. 396, which states that representations can be taken to have rank-many rows. Exact rational row reduction has polynomial bit complexity for an already polynomial-bit matrix. Rational entries and integer entries are equivalent for this polynomial-bit existence question: multiplying each row by a common denominator preserves column independence and increases bit length by at most a polynomial in the original total encoding length. These normalizations are audit explanations, not public solution hints or a demand for the original randomized construction.

Downloaded/read actual publisher MFCS2025 paper as transversal-rep-mfcs2025.pdf/.txt. Publisher metadata gives 20 August 2025. Intro/Thm1 PDF p. 4 explicitly keep deterministic polynomial representation open and give rational representations in r^{O(log r)} N^{O(1)} time. §1.2 p. 5 distinguishes a single matrix from a family of union representations; the latter is not the card target. Read Thm1 proof p. 13 and application statements pp. 13–14.

Source discrepancy: Thm1 on MFCS2025 PDF pp. 4 and13 states entry bit length r^{O(log r)} without N, but its proof on p. 13 concludes r^{O(log r)} N^{O(1)} bits. The sharper n-independent assertion cannot hold at fixed rank with unboundedly many distinct nonparallel columns, e.g. rank-2 uniform matroids: choosing two independent matrix rows gives an injective projection of the column span, and bounded-bit rational coordinates give only finitely many possibilities. The public card therefore reports only the supported overall (N+2)^{O(log(N+2))} time and output-length bound. This discrepancy affects the sharper entry bound, not the polynomial-versus-quasipolynomial endpoint; no independent full-proof or Lean verification is claimed.

Downloaded/read actual 2603.17345v1 (18 March 2026), Huang–Kakimura–Kobayashi–Terao, Polynomial Kernels with Reachability for Weighted d-Matroid Intersection, as transversal-rep-kernels2026.pdf/.txt. Abstract/PDF p. 1 and §4/Theorem3 PDF p. 11 concern randomized reachable kernels from bipartite presentations of transversal matroids. This is not a deterministic polynomial-bit construction of one rational representation. It does not resolve the target and is retained in the bounded scope audit rather than added as unrelated public progress.

Bounded primary searches through 16 September 2026 found no verified polynomial-time construction or impossibility theorem. The 2025 primary paper directly states the remaining problem; the 2026 result above concerns a different output. Generic PIT, symbolic determinant identity tests, bipartite realization from explicit matroid bases, and representations of q-matroids are not identified with this simultaneous rational-matrix construction. No equivalence to general PIT or circuit lower bounds is claimed.

The mathematical matrix property is expressed through all subsets and all rational coefficient families, with rank-zero and empty-ground-set conventions specified. The algorithmic quantifiers are one finite program and fixed polynomial constants before every graph. The negation ranges over all such programs and bounds, with an adversarial graph allowed to depend on them; it does not incorrectly ask for a nonrepresentable transversal matroid.

The active Almost 2-SAT kernel card TCS-6749 is related through the representation applications described in the 2025 source, but is a different mathematical target. Preserve the existing relation; no automatic merge or source-driven category move is proposed.
